title: Jehu Announces Judgment on Baasha
image_prompt: Biblical historical realism in the northern kingdom of Israel. Jehu son of Hanani, a solemn prophet, confronts the royal house with the LORD’s judgment because Baasha followed Jeroboam’s sins and provoked the LORD. Show a guarded palace court, royal officials listening uneasily, the prophet standing without fear, and the contrast between royal power and prophetic authority. Ancient Israelite clothing, oil lamps, stone walls, no modern objects.

title: Elah Falls and Zimri Takes the Throne
image_prompt: In Tirzah, King Elah drinks in the house of Arza while Zimri, commander of part of the chariots, stages a coup. Convey the sudden change of power through tense palace corridors, startled attendants, and soldiers switching allegiance; avoid graphic violence. Outside, Israel’s army is encamped against Gibbethon and has not yet heard that the throne has changed.

title: Zimri’s Seven-Day Reign
image_prompt: At Tirzah, Zimri is proclaimed king while the army besieging Gibbethon hears of the coup. Omri and the troops turn back toward Tirzah, surround the city, and Zimri’s position collapses. Show rival banners, soldiers approaching the fortified city, and a king isolated inside the royal complex; communicate the brief, unstable reign without depicting explicit injury.

title: Omri Prevails and Builds Samaria
image_prompt: Israel is divided between supporters of Tibni and Omri. Show two rival camps separated across a rocky valley, followed by Omri’s faction gaining control after Tibni’s death. Omri purchases the hill of Samaria and establishes a new capital; workers survey the hilltop and raise the first walls and buildings. Include the political uncertainty and the city’s strategic high ground.

title: Ahab, Jezebel, and the Rebuilding of Jericho
image_prompt: Ahab son of Omri rules from Samaria and does more evil than those before him. Show Ahab’s marriage to Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, and the promotion of Baal worship through a conspicuous shrine and altar. In a secondary visual beat, Hiel of Bethel begins rebuilding Jericho; the fulfillment of Joshua’s curse is suggested by mourners and an unfinished building site, with no graphic depiction.

title: Elijah Announces the Drought
image_prompt: Elijah the Tishbite, rugged and plainly dressed, stands before Ahab and declares that there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word. The king’s officials react with disbelief and alarm. Contrast the rich royal court with the prophet’s austere appearance; through a window show parched fields, dry streambeds, and a cloudless sky.

title: The Widow of Zarephath Shares Her Last Food
image_prompt: Near Zarephath, a widow gathers sticks while her son waits nearby. Elijah asks for water and a small cake; she explains that she has only a handful of meal and a little oil. Show her small clay jar, nearly empty flour vessel, modest hearth, and the difficult decision to offer hospitality. After she acts in faith, the meal and oil continue to supply the household day after day.

title: Elijah Prays and the Widow’s Son Lives
image_prompt: The widow’s son falls gravely ill and appears lifeless; keep the scene solemn and non-graphic. Elijah carries him to an upper room, lays him on the bed, and pleads with the LORD. The mother waits in anguish at the doorway. The child is restored, and the widow confesses that Elijah is a man of God and that the LORD’s word is true.

title: Obadiah Meets Elijah
image_prompt: After the long drought, the LORD tells Elijah to present himself to Ahab. Obadiah, Ahab’s steward who secretly hid one hundred prophets in caves and supplied them with bread and water during Jezebel’s persecution, meets Elijah while searching for grass and water. Show exhausted servants, dry hills, empty streams, and Obadiah’s anxiety that Ahab will punish him if Elijah disappears again.

title: Elijah Challenges Baal on Mount Carmel
image_prompt: On Mount Carmel, Elijah confronts Ahab and the gathered Israelites, asking how long they will halt between two opinions. Two altars are prepared, one for Baal and one for the LORD; a bull is placed on each, but no fire is lit by human hands. Show the rocky ridge, the assembled crowd, Baal’s prophets, and Elijah proposing that the God who answers by fire is the true God.

title: Baal’s Prophets Call in Vain
image_prompt: From morning until the time of the evening offering, Baal’s prophets call to their god and circle their altar. Elijah watches and challenges their silence. Emphasize the hot sun, dust, exhaustion, and the crowd’s growing uncertainty; avoid graphic ritual detail and keep the scene historically grounded.

title: Fire Falls on Elijah’s Sacrifice
image_prompt: Elijah repairs the LORD’s altar with twelve stones representing Israel’s tribes, arranges the wood and sacrifice, and has water poured repeatedly until the trench fills. He prays that the people may know the LORD is God. Fire from heaven consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust, and water. The people fall facedown and confess that the LORD is God. Render the supernatural fire reverently, not as a modern explosion.

title: Rain Returns to Israel
image_prompt: The people seize Baal’s prophets and take them to the brook Kishon; show the aftermath without graphic violence. Elijah climbs Carmel and prays, sending his servant repeatedly to look toward the sea. A small cloud appears, the sky darkens, and heavy rain falls across the dry land. Elijah runs ahead of Ahab’s chariot toward Jezreel; rain-soaked earth and renewed streams signal relief.

title: Elijah Flees and Is Strengthened
image_prompt: Jezebel threatens Elijah after hearing of Carmel. Elijah flees into the wilderness, sits beneath a broom tree, and, exhausted and afraid, asks that his life may end. Portray his distress compassionately and non-graphically, without romanticizing despair. An angel touches him and provides a cake baked on coals and a jar of water; he eats, rests, and receives strength for the journey to Horeb.

title: The Still Small Voice at Horeb
image_prompt: At Mount Horeb, Elijah shelters in a cave and hears the LORD ask why he is there. A mighty wind tears at the mountain, then an earthquake and fire pass, but the LORD’s message comes in a still small voice. Show Elijah listening at the cave entrance with his mantle partly covering his face; the vast mountain landscape becomes quiet after the storm.

title: Elijah Receives His Next Commission
image_prompt: The LORD instructs Elijah concerning Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha, and reveals that seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal. Show Elijah listening intently in the rugged wilderness, with distant roads or silhouettes hinting at the future missions. Do not imply that all three anointings occur in this scene.

title: Elisha Is Called from the Plow
image_prompt: Elijah finds Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and casts his mantle upon him. Elisha asks to bid farewell to his parents, then sacrifices the oxen, uses the plowing equipment as fuel, and shares the meat with the people before following Elijah. Show the field, oxen, wooden plow, mantle, and family farewell with realistic rural detail.

title: Ben-hadad Threatens Samaria
image_prompt: Ben-hadad of Syria gathers a large army and demands Ahab’s silver, gold, wives, and children. Ahab initially agrees, but refuses when the demands expand to his servants’ houses and possessions. Show Samaria’s fortified walls, Syrian tents and chariots beyond the city, tense messengers, and Ahab consulting Israel’s elders.

title: Israel Surprises the Syrian Camp
image_prompt: A prophet tells Ahab that the LORD will deliver the great Syrian host into Israel’s hand so Israel may know Him. Young provincial leaders lead a sortie, followed by the army. Show disciplined movement from Samaria’s gate, dust, shields, and a surprised Syrian camp scattering; keep battle non-graphic and emphasize the reversal of expectations.

title: The Syrians Return and Are Defeated Again
image_prompt: The prophet warns Ahab that Syria will return the next year. Syrian advisers claim Israel’s God is a god of the hills, so they choose the plain. The armies face each other, and the man of God promises victory. Israel defeats the Syrians; survivors retreat to Aphek, where a wall collapses on many. Convey the battle’s scale without graphic injuries.

title: Ahab Makes a Treaty with Ben-hadad
image_prompt: Ben-hadad’s servants approach Ahab wearing sackcloth and ropes as signs of submission. Ahab calls Ben-hadad his brother, receives him into his chariot, and makes a treaty allowing cities to be returned and trading quarters established. Show wary diplomacy after battle, a guarded royal meeting, and the political compromise that will later be condemned.

title: A Prophet Condemns Ahab for Sparing Ben-hadad
image_prompt: A prophet asks another man to strike him, and when the man refuses, a lion kills him; the detail establishes the seriousness of the prophetic command. Another man wounds the prophet at his request, allowing him to disguise himself with a bandage and confront Ahab through a parable about a prisoner entrusted to a soldier. Ahab recognizes the judgment against himself for releasing Ben-hadad, and he returns to Samaria sullen and displeased. Keep the wound and the lion incident non-graphic; focus on the prophet’s parable and Ahab’s troubled response.

title: Naboth Refuses to Sell His Vineyard
image_prompt: Naboth’s vineyard lies beside Ahab’s palace in Jezreel. Ahab offers another vineyard or money, but Naboth refuses because the land is his ancestral inheritance. Ahab returns home troubled, lies on his bed, turns his face away, and refuses food. Jezebel asks what is wrong and promises to obtain the vineyard. Show stone vineyard boundaries, vines, the palace garden, and the conflict between royal desire and covenant inheritance.

title: Elijah Confronts Ahab in the Vineyard
image_prompt: The LORD sends Elijah to meet Ahab in Naboth’s vineyard. Elijah declares judgment on Ahab’s house for the king’s wrongdoing and Jezebel’s wickedness. Show Ahab standing among the vines as Elijah confronts him, with palace attendants held at a distance. The prophecy concerns future judgment; do not depict future events as already occurring.

title: Ahab Humbles Himself
image_prompt: The narrative describes Ahab’s exceptional wickedness and Jezebel’s influence. When Ahab hears Elijah’s words, he tears his clothes, wears sackcloth, fasts, and walks softly. The LORD acknowledges his humility and postpones disaster on Ahab’s house until his son’s days. Show the king’s repentance in a quiet chamber, sackcloth against royal surroundings, and the prophet departing.

title: Ahab and Jehoshaphat Plan War
image_prompt: After three years without war between Syria and Israel, Ahab proposes retaking Ramoth-gilead. Jehoshaphat of Judah agrees to join him but asks to inquire of the LORD. About four hundred prophets give a favorable answer; Zedekiah makes horns of iron as a symbolic demonstration. Show both kings in royal robes at Samaria’s gate, advisers arranged around them, and the prophetic display.

title: Micaiah Reveals the Unwelcome Truth
image_prompt: The messenger urges Micaiah to agree with the other prophets, but Micaiah insists he will speak what the LORD tells him. He first echoes the crowd ironically, then declares that Israel will be scattered like sheep without a shepherd. Micaiah describes a heavenly council and a lying spirit deceiving Ahab’s prophets. Show the heavenly vision as a reverent, distinct symbolic scene, not modern fantasy.

title: Micaiah Is Struck and Imprisoned
image_prompt: Zedekiah strikes Micaiah and challenges his prophecy. Micaiah answers that Zedekiah will know the truth when he hides in an inner chamber. Ahab orders Micaiah imprisoned on bread and water until the king returns safely. Show the prophet calm and resolute as guards escort him away while the kings prepare for battle.

title: Ahab Dies at Ramoth-gilead
image_prompt: Ahab disguises himself while Jehoshaphat wears royal robes. A Syrian archer shoots at random and strikes Ahab between the joints of his armor. The king remains propped in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening, then dies. Show the battle from a respectful distance, the chariot returning to Samaria, and the washing of blood from it at the pool where dogs gather, fulfilling the prophecy; no graphic injury.

title: Jehoshaphat’s Reign and the Failed Ships
image_prompt: Jehoshaphat rules Judah and does what is right, though the high places remain. Show him overseeing the kingdom and its people. At Ezion-geber, ships intended to sail to Ophir are wrecked before departure; Jehoshaphat refuses Ahaziah’s offer to join a new venture. Close with the transition to his son Jehoram.

title: Ahaziah Continues Ahab’s Sins
image_prompt: Ahaziah son of Ahab becomes king in Samaria and continues the sins of Jeroboam, serving Baal and provoking the LORD. Show the royal court with Baal worship symbols in the background and a spiritually divided kingdom. This closing panel should lead visually into the opening of 2 Kings.
